notes: final-full.csv, final-build-final.csv, checks.log, build.log, differential.txt, current-membership-profile.txt, frames.txt, memory files and source.json refer to the final source, including normalized-parent-path depth accounting.

final-repeat.csv and final-reverse.csv retain the pre-classification M18 build, not the final executable. Its full run is separately retained as pre-classification-full.csv. final-membership-profile.txt and final-nested-profile.txt also refer to that pre-classification build.

parent-before/after/final CSVs compare successive demanded-parent prototypes: copied row frames, shared row frames, then immutable replay-safe Parent reads. They precede alias hardening and nested focus/depth regressions, which do not affect these timed workload shapes. Reproduce the before stage by replacing Row::scoped shared binding construction with child plus per-binding bind; mark Parent as effectful. The shared stage changes only frame sharing.

The nonrecursive CopiedValue shape helper and moving the Copied value variant were discarded. Patches and raw samples preserve the negative experiments; no such code remains. after-fold-profile.txt remains under target only because it profiles the discarded helper, not the final engine.

retained-storage-classification.diff replaces chained predicates and recursive copy type checks with one direct-storage match. It adds no metadata or specialized workload path. Forward and reverse pairs improve membership 7-8%; the final membership sample no longer outlines is_array/is_object.

No input index, universal ancestry allocation, new execution-plan instruction or JIT. A local transform change map indexes changed identities/ranges only. Parent capture uses generated immutable lexical slots on demanded paths.

Transform views preserve borrowed raw/static leaves; dynamic containers copy member lists to break aliases. Unscoped mutation/custom cloners/function-valued or cyclic updates are explicit compatibility boundaries, with errors rather than approximation.

Full-run composition folds are 14-15% below M17, but the final 300 ms reverse-order pairs are 1-5% above. Final pairs still show 2-3% fold losses, about 6% tiny empty/descendant losses, and 2% membership loss. Profiles confirm existing hot routines; they do not establish causality for every residual code-generation difference.
The Node::run stack frame is 1072 bytes in M17 and 1040 bytes in final M18. Timed source is identified by hashes.
